note.question: How can the price-setting newsvendor problem with limited demand information be represented using sample-based?
note.overview: The model considers a price-setting newsvendor problem in which the demand distribution is unknown. We assume that the retailer exercises only a few price points with a sample set of demand realizations for each exercised price. Given this limited demand information, we define an ambiguity set and study two robust optimization models that maximize the worst-case profit (maxmin profit) and minimize the maximum regret (minmax regret), respectively.

For each price p, the seller faces a random demand D(p), which is a price-dependent random variable.
